summary:
plan.md is written: the twin-leg Art Deco south tower (fluted, stepped legs; four portal struts with stepped, recessed frames; an X brace under the deck; red-lit caps over the cable saddles) on a grey pier inside an elliptical fender. The deck module tiles every 16 blocks with a Warren truss, an orange railing and lamps. Both cable modules follow the given curves to half a block (slab on top), with cable bands and thin red suspender lines. It reads as the Golden Gate from the tower outline, the International Orange (terracotta), the cable curves and the suspender rows; every block id passes the check, but nothing was built or rendered. Golden Gate kit in four modules: plot 0 Art Deco south tower on pier/fender with fluted legs, four stepped portal struts, X brace, saddle caps; plot 1 tiling deck section; plots 2 and 3 catenary cables with suspenders.
All International Orange terracotta/concrete per the architect's exact tables; no interiors.

tower massing: parts/tower.mjs builds the tower massing from the plan's coordinates. It has the fender ring, pier, both legs in four stages, tie beam, X brace, plain lower strut, four framed struts with haunches, crown, and saddle caps with aircraft lights. make.sh gives a whole build.nbt with 10272 cells and no refused or off-palette writes.
polish: No render was looked at; I only ran mcd check (0 floating, 0 orphans), spot-checked cells (shroomlight at 23,114,11 not re-read after the last edit) and did not run fit.
Plan ticks (plan.md checklist, elements.md) not updated.
Walkways and red_concrete accents on the lower strut faces are left to the deck and skin parts.
Fender and pier lanterns and the lower strut's red_concrete faces are left for the trim and skin parts.

waste.what: Ticking plan.md and elements.md checklists by hand (BSD sed failed)
waste.tool: a tick helper script, e.g. mcd tick <part>

summary:
tower skin: Tower skin (P2) builds only the setback ledges: 48 bottom smooth_red_sandstone_slab courses at S1→S2 (y 55) and S2→S3 (y 80), both legs, in air.
Flutes, bands, strut frames and panels, and lamp panels are NOT built: their cells are P1's solid steel, and runParts refuses writes into earlier parts' cells.
make.sh writes a whole build.nbt; the tower skin line shows 48 placed, 0 refused, 0 off-palette; `mcd check` reports 0 floating and 0 unsupported.
polish: Riveted fluting on all four leg faces (fluteFace): blocked, cells owned by the massing (P1).
Orange bands y 6..7, 53..54, 78..79, 103..104, 111 (bandCourse): blocked, cells owned by the massing (P1).
Strut recessed frames, raised orange_concrete panels and strut-top shroomlights (portalStrut frame:true): blocked, cells owned by the massing (P1).
Lamp panels: shroomlight at x 18 / x 28, z 11..12, y 40..41: blocked, inside the massing's legs.
Fix belongs in P1 (parts/tower.mjs): leave the recess front cells, band rows and strut frame fronts out of legStage/portalStrut, or run the skin inside the massing part. Recorded in plan.md Notes.
Not visually checked: no render of the ledges (48 one-block slabs), and no `mcd fit` run.

waste.what: Checking which of the skin's cells were already solid cost a full make.sh run to discover: the massing's legs, bands, strut frames and lamp cells are locked, so the skin's recesses and bands were refused by the build library, not by any check I could run in advance.
waste.cost: One make.sh run plus reading runParts' lock code (about 6 tool calls).
waste.tool: A `mcd lock-map` or `runParts --dry-run` that lists which cells an earlier part owns, and a warning from a part's helper when its target cells are already owned, before any write.

waste.what: The ledge cell lists (x/z ranges per setback, mirrored to the east leg at x' = 46 - x) were worked out by hand from the SITE table.
waste.cost: About 10 minutes of cell-by-cell reasoning, 48 cells.
waste.tool: A `ledgeCells`-style helper in vocab/h2.mjs that takes a leg stage pair and returns the outside-footprint ring at a given y, with the east mirror built in.

companions.task: Lay the fluted leg faces and the bands by hand on the massing's steel once the massing leaves the recess and band cells open (the actual exclusion work).
Set the shroomlight lamp panels and strut-top lights into the open strut frames and inner leg faces.

summary:
deck: parts/deck.mjs built: plot 1 deck section (x 48..62, z 0..15, tiling), plot 0 deck through the tower (full section z 0..7 and 16..23, road and floor beams through the portal at z 8..15) and both cantilevered walkways.
make.sh wrote a whole build.nbt; the deck line reports 1646 placed with no REFUSED or OFF-PALETTE blocks. mcd render shows the portal deck and walkways reading correctly.
Lamps are left to the trim part (P5), as elements.md assigns them. Ticked elements.md items for the plot 0 deck, walkways and plot 1 section.
polish: Plot 1 deck is a floating group in isolation (check reports 694 floating cells at x 48..62); it is supported only once the repeated copies and the cables are composed, so this is expected for a kit module.
mcd check flags Warren zig-zag peaks at y 36 (x 16/30, z 2/6/18) as orphans; that is the spec's Warren pattern (peak touches the chord above only), not a fault to fix here.
mcd check reports 'walkable end to end: false' along z; I did not investigate it. mcd walk from the entrance is ok (448 cells reached).
I did not run mcd fit; only check and render were run.
plan.md has no checkbox list; the ticks went into elements.md, which holds the checklist.
Deck lamp pairs (z 8 of each 16 in plot 1) and the walkway lamps are not placed here; they belong to parts/trim.mjs.

waste.what: Read deckSection and walkway source to confirm the xOff semantics (additive offset, so plot 1 is PLOT_X.deck and plot 0 is TOWER_DECK_X) and that walkway defaults to WALK_ANCHOR.
waste.cost: 2 Read calls, about 1 minute of the budget
waste.tool: a one-line note in plan.md or base.mjs stating that deckSection xOff is the additive plot origin (48 for plot 1, 16 for plot 0)

waste.what: Checked each part's orphan and floating reports by hand against the spec's Warren pattern and the plot 1 floating group, since check cannot tell a kit module's intended floating from a real fault.
waste.cost: 1 check run plus reasoning, about 2 minutes
waste.tool: mcd check with a per-part or kit-module flag that marks a module as composed later, so floating and orphan warnings for it are suppressed

waste.what: Ticked elements.md items by hand with a separate Read and three Edit calls, while plan.md has no checkbox list at all.
waste.tool: a tick command (for example a script that reads the part name and ticks the matching elements.md lines) and a checkbox list in plan.md so the instruction matches the file

companions.task: Check the Warren truss diagonals and the portal-deck connection at the legs, and confirm the floor beams and lateral bracing are built the way a real truss is.
Design the orange railing along the edge girders (the red_sandstone_wall run at y 39 and its post and gap rhythm) so it reads as the bridge's railing rather than a plain wall line.
Lay the road surface and lane markings (gray_concrete with the yellow centre line and white dashes) and check the dash rhythm against the spec's z 0..3 and 8..11 positions.

summary:
cables: parts/cables.mjs builds plot 2 (main span, z 0..248, catenary y(z) with cableCell body/slab and orange_concrete bands at z%4=0, 63 suspender rows from y 40 to the cable) and plot 3 (side span, z 0..231, the u-polynomial to z 171 then level y 36, ropes z 12..168 stepping down 40/39/38/37/36).
make.sh runs whole: cables placed 7568 cells, no REFUSED writes, no off-palette blocks. mcd fit is OK; spot checks match the catenary heights and rope extents.
Cables sit at PLOT_X.mainCable (63) and PLOT_X.sideCable (78) plus local x 0 and 14, as base.mjs defines.
polish: mcd check reports the cables as FLOATING (3 groups: x 63 and 77 main, x 78 and 92 side). This is expected for a kit module: the cables hang free until placement joins them to the tower top, the anchorage and the deck, so nothing in this part can fix it.

The slab rule is applied as written (slab only where f - floor(f) >= 0.5). That gives no slab at main z 0 (f 45.48) or side z 0 (f 112.48), where plan.md's SITE text says '+ slab'. Recorded in plan.md Notes; the plan's wording should be confirmed.

Plot x: base.mjs PLOT_X.mainCable = 63 (cables 63 and 77), while the system kit text puts plot 2 at x 62..76. I followed base.mjs; plot 1 deck is at PLOT_X.deck 48, so the two layouts disagree by one cell and the reconciliation belongs to the placement step.

The cables are one block wide (2 m at 0.5 blocks/m); in the front elevation they read as thin lines. That is the spec's single-cell line, but the cable may need a second cell for weight, which the plan doesn't ask for.

waste.what: Checked each cable column by hand with an ad hoc node script (listing body and slab y per z, rope extents at sample z). Several expected values had to be recomputed from the catenary formulas to tell real errors from my own arithmetic slips.
waste.cost: about 3 script runs and 2 corrections to expected values; no blocks placed by hand
waste.tool: a `mcd cable-check build.nbt --x 63,77 --z 0..248 --profile main` (or a generic 'list the y-range per column per z' report with 8-connectivity and rope-gap checks) would replace the ad hoc script; a plan-level 'expected y(z)' table would let the check compare automatically

waste.what: Converted the catenary formulas from the plan into per-z cell heights and slab decisions by reasoning, not by a shared helper; the same formula appears twice (main and side).
waste.cost: about 250 + 232 z values reasoned from the formula; a few rounding decisions on the slab threshold
waste.tool: cableCell already encodes the slab rule; a `cableLine(g, x, z0, z1, heightFn, opts)` helper (mentioned in elements.md but absent from vocab) would own the loop, the band rule and the rope placement

companions.task: Hang and tension the suspender ropes: confirm the plot 2 rope tops sit exactly one block under each cable body, and that the plot 3 rope bottoms step down with the side-span railing.
Connect the free cables to the saddle housings on the tower top and to the anchorage pylon, so the 'floating' groups the check reports become one structure in placement.

summary: lights and trim: parts/trim.mjs is built: plot 1 deck lamp pairs at z 8, a seam lantern per tile, plot 0 walkway lamps, pier and fender lanterns; make.sh writes a whole build.nbt.
polish: seam lantern refused until the deck sidewalk lands
walkway lamp shafts float until the deck walkway platforms land

summary: inspection: walk ok and fit OK, nothing to fix
